decisions.executionNote: Target board shows a cream dog with brown ears. Begin left basket approach, raising and pitching gripper toward a downward grasp while right remains clear.
Finish downward orientation and advance left above the moving basket. Basket is translating right, so track modestly right without crossing workspace.
Replan after continuity guard with smaller pose increments. Aim for the basket's left side rim, allowing the fingers to straddle that wall while tracking the belt.
Close left fingers around the visible basket side rim, then begin a cautious vertical retention test. Judge basket motion in the cameras rather than gripper command.
Basket was not retained; fingers closed in front of it. Reopen and advance farther along its left wall, tracking rightward while remaining in left workspace.
Guard interrupted forward motion. Lower the left wrist with very small forward increments to stay on the continuous elbow-up branch and bring the open fingers around the rim.
Basket is slipping forward of the fingertips. Advance to straddle the left wall, close, and test a small lift; keep left x negative and right stationary.
No prior step executed. Use millimetric increments and a slight forward tilt to reduce the IK change, then close on the left side wall.
Basket has moved into the right workspace and left fingers appear empty. Release and retreat left; start right-arm basket approach so the left arm can later pick the incoming dog.
Both proposed starts were rejected. Halve retreat and approach increments to maintain joint continuity; right begins preparation while left opens and withdraws.
Advance right toward basket's right wall with an angled downward approach; move left back into the incoming dog's workspace, without crossing.
Right approaches basket rim with forward-angled fingers to avoid excessive reach; left stages above the matching cream-and-brown dog but does not grasp before basket lift.
Bring right fingers farther along the basket's right wall and close while tracking belt motion; left aligns to the incoming dog and stays open.
Test basket retention by lifting right 12 cm with a slight retreat. Left tracks the dog forward while open, pending confirmation that the basket is lifted.
Basket retention is uncertain: it receded in the wrist view. Reopen above the rim and advance before lowering, rather than pushing its wall. Left continues tracking the dog open.
Shift right gripper laterally onto the basket's right side rim, rather than its front span; close and make a short retention test. Left follows dog while open.
Lift the newly closed right grasp 10 cm with retreat to preserve elbow configuration; verify basket follows. Keep left dog alignment open.
Basket remained on belt: prior closure was over the interior/front rim. Correct laterally to the actual right wall while descending from above and tracking belt motion.
Rejected start moved neither arm. Reduce initial lowering and ramp gently while approaching the basket's right side from above.
Move right fingers forward and down to the actual wall height; earlier closures were too high or inside the basket. Keep left open on the dog until basket lift is established.
Latest descent was interrupted. Reorient right closing direction around its approach axis to pinch the visible front rim, keeping wrist translation very small and configuration continuous.
Right open jaws now visibly span the slanted rim. Close without translation, then make a small inward/upward retention test while left tracks the target.
Only closure executed. Retreat gently before raising to restore reach margin, maintaining right closure and checking whether the rim follows.
Rejected retreat moved neither arm. Reduce to 1–2 mm straight retreat with right closed to get away from the sensitive IK region before lifting.
Right now has better reach margin. Make a six-centimeter lift/retreat test with the rim at the closed tips; left remains open and follows the matching dog.
Basket did not follow the lift. Lower the open right gripper substantially toward the actual low rim and advance to it; previous closures were above it. Track dog with left.
Basket corner is now between the open jaws at near-rim height. Make a small final descent/advance, close, and test retention with an 8 mm lift.
Only three approach steps executed. Close at this rim-straddling pose and ramp a small inward retreat/lift to respect the sensitive IK region.
Right rim grasp again slipped. Approach lower with a shallower angle; secure the identified dog in left workspace before it drifts across the center, then continue basket recovery.
Hold the dog closed. Right fingertips are now at the estimated front wall height; close while tracking briefly, then test a 2.4 cm lift and inward retreat.
Dog remains visibly retained. Basket is still moving right; reopen and advance toward its nearer left corner at lower height, using a shallower approach to keep reach manageable.
Continuity guard stopped the forward reach. Use a small downward adjustment and aim the approach axis diagonally toward the basket without extending the wrist farther right.
Close at the low basket corner and test an inward pull without lifting; keep the dog retained and both arms on their own sides.
Inward pull was empty. Advance the open right fingers along the basket's nearer side, lowering for reach margin and undoing the roll so jaws can pinch its wall.
Forward approach hit the continuity limit. Redirect reach laterally toward the basket while retracting in y, aiming the tool diagonally right and maintaining the held dog.
The basket is farther forward than the fingertips. Use a shallow approach and millimetric forward corrections, retaining continuity and watching for the reach guard.
Forward correction approached the extension boundary. Retreat inward and lower along the near side of the belt to regain configuration margin before attempting the basket's low corner.
Replan from actual right pose after failed IK. Retract from the conveyor while moving laterally along the reach arc, maintaining a margin rather than pressing farther forward.
Basket has moved beyond safe reach. Withdraw right rather than extend into the boundary, and lift the visibly held dog clear of incoming objects while monitoring the belt.
Rejected retreat executed nothing. Ramp smaller inward increments for right; left lifts the retained dog away from belt traffic.
Return right to a central, elbow-up ready pose without crossing. Keep the target held left and monitor whether the basket becomes reachable again.
